<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, touching **115** documentable anchor(s).

**60** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **76** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f6bde74ea9d4e5472ef1cbc2639db477f08b8328` — the merge of head `de8d869b456ea23cfc625ebd528f0c42601278f7` into base `3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f6bde74ea9d4e5472ef1cbc2639db477f08b8328 && git checkout f6bde74ea9d4e5472ef1cbc2639db477f08b8328
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606 de8d869b456ea23cfc625ebd528f0c42601278f7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606 && git merge --no-ff de8d869b456ea23cfc625ebd528f0c42601278f7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3c038eb152d29117b4eccfc2910e8913361fb606` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Check-runs at the read: 56 success, 10 skipped, `Check Changeset` failure (the declared correction, judged in ②), `Test Core (9/10)` and `Test Core (10/10)` still in progress. This record judges the design; those two shards had not concluded.

### ① Derived judgments

- `POST /reset-password`, `POST /phone-number/reset-password`: the success body is unchanged; a success now also writes `revoked: true` on the account's unrevoked `sys_api_key` rows and deletes its non-`credential` `sys_account` rows. New failure answer: a 5xx after the password is written, when the ending cannot be read or written. Right as a narrowing, and declared. Two gaps in it are S3 and S4.
- `POST /change-password`: answer unchanged, nothing ended; one new best-effort mail. Right.
- `POST /admin/set-user-password`: `revoked` gains `signInAccounts`, the ledger row gains `revokedSignInAccounts`; with the switch off nothing is ended. Additive, right. The exact-shape pins and the dogfood key list are moved with it.
- `os user set-password`: `OperatorPasswordResetOutcome` (exported from the package index) gains the required field `signInAccountsUnlinked`; its one consumer in the tree, the CLI command, is in the diff. Additive for a reader, right.
- `GET /verify-email`: the accept-set narrows for a token without `updateTo` on a deployment with `autoSignInAfterVerification: true`; with it off, unchanged. Right, and pinned with its control.
- `GET /magic-link/verify`: narrows for a link whose stored row predates the change. The identifier `magic-link:TOKEN`, the plain default and `plugin.options.storeToken` being the caller's raw option all match the vendor file; the replaced token reaches the vendor's own `INVALID_TOKEN` redirect. Right.
- `readCredentialChangedAt`: a credential row never written over, created onto an account that already existed, now reads as a change. Every reader of the clock narrows with it (email-change links, second-factor challenges, the two link doors). Right as the rule states it; its discriminator is S1.
- `CredentialClockReader` gains `findUserById`; `ENDED_EMAIL_CHANGE_TOKEN` and `endEmailChangeTokenIssuedBeforeCredentialChange` are renamed. None is exported from the package index, and no other reference remains in `packages/` or `content/`. No public surface moves. Right.
- `BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` 32 to 36 and the ninth name in `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE.email_template`: both objectql pins move with it. Right; see N3.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on plugin-auth, plugin-email, core and cli, with the BREAKING banner, both declaration lines and one ADR-0087 marker in the changeset body. This matches the Post-Task rule for a non-protocol breaking change. objectql carries test-only edits and is rightly absent. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right: every behaviour change above refuses or ends something that was admitted before.
- The DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/credential-change-ends-prior-access.md` is right and complete. The deleted sentence ("An account's first password is not a change.") is false on this head for a first password set onto an existing account. No other sentence of that note is made false: its four bullets and its BREAKING paragraph still hold, and "an account that never changed its local password" stays true under the new reading. The new changeset states the replacement rule. This same-head record confirms the correction.
- One sentence of the new changeset does not match the tree: S5.

### ③ Boundary flags

- SQL push-down. `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts` reads the linked accounts through the vendor adapter's `findAccounts` and deletes by id through `deleteAccount`; the reason is given (the account-delete hooks run, and the in-memory adapter is served). The key arm reads ids with `user_id` and `revoked` pushed into the `where`, then writes per id; the count of rows really written and the read-twice check are the stated reason. `forced-reset-revocation.ts` keeps its per-row shape for the same outcome contract, but filters `provider_id` in the application: N2. No join is built in memory.
- Open question (PR body), `revoked_reason` on a reset's keys: answered for this PR. The field is a closed set on `sys_api_key`, so a new value is a platform-objects change; shipping without one is consistent with the restore guard as it stands. Held with the private residuals.
- Escalated to the seat: a reset's unlink writes no unlink record (the `account.delete.before` hook records one only on `/unlink-account`, verified), so re-linking is left to the implicit-link gates in `implicit-account-linking.ts`. A user's own unlink is honoured by that record; a reset's is not. Whether a reset records it is a ruling, not a defect of this diff.
- Escalated to the seat: the tree names three code-and-link sign-in doors (`SECOND_FACTOR_CODE_AND_LINK_DOOR_PATHS`). This PR puts two on the credential clock, as its rule says; `/phone-number/verify` is not on it.
- Escalated to the seat: the module's list (keys, linked sign-in accounts, passkeys) is narrower than the tree's own enumeration of an account's standing grants (`USER_KEYED_STORES`, `USER_ROW_COLUMNS` in `invitation-mailbox-proof.ts`).
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R6 — graded in the seat's private notes; none blocks this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`, `readCredentialChangedAt`: "created together with the account" is judged by a 1 s wall-clock window between `sys_user.created_at` and the credential row's creation. In the vendor's sign-up, `createUser` awaits `user.create.after` (the host hook, `settleMembership`, `settleSelfRegistrationGrant`) before `linkAccount` stamps the row; an administrator's create-user also hashes in between. A creation whose hooks take longer than 1 s reads as a change at sign-up. On a deployment with `autoSignInAfterVerification: true`, the verification link that sign-up mails carries an `iat` in whole seconds, so it then answers `INVALID_TOKEN`. The new tests advance a fake clock and cannot see this. Remedy: have the doors that set a password onto an existing account mark the change, or judge creation by something other than elapsed time.
S2 (should-fix) — `auth-manager-after-hook.ts`: `endOrRemindWhatTheAccountAdded` runs ahead of the ADR-0069 D1 block. When a reset's ending throws, the password is written but `stampPasswordChangedAt` and `recordPasswordHistory` never run for it. Remedy: write the stamp and the history entry before the step that can throw.
S3 (should-fix) — `auth-manager-after-hook.ts`: when a completed reset cannot name its account (`RESET_DOOR_SUBJECT` absent because the before-hook's read answered `ok: false`), the hook logs and returns, and the reset answers success with nothing ended. The module header says a read that fails is not swallowed. Remedy: answer the error there too.
S4 (should-fix) — `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts`, `unrevokedApiKeys`: the read selects `revoked: false`. The admission seam (`core/src/security/api-key.ts`) refuses only `revoked === true || 1`, and `sys-api-key.object.ts` says "a null `revoked` reads as live". A row with a null flag is admitted and is not ended by a reset. The forced-reset arm reads the same way. Remedy: select every row whose flag is not true.
S5 (should-fix) — `.changeset/password-reset-ends-added-access.md`, BREAKING paragraph: "is refused as an unknown key". The seam answers a revoked key with the located refusal `403 API_KEY_REVOKED`; "unknown keys keep the generic 401". The test asserts only that the key is not admitted. Remedy: name the answer the seam gives. `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` repeats the sentence (prose, the seat's).
N1 (nit) — `readCredentialChangedAt`: the comparison of `created - accountCreated` against the window accepts any negative difference. A row stamped before its account reads as created with it; bound both sides.
N2 (nit) — `forced-reset-revocation.ts`: the `provider_id` filter could sit in the `where`. The arm deletes through `engine.delete` while the self-service path deletes through the vendor adapter, so the account-delete hooks run on one road only. On the self-service road a host `account.delete.before` that answers `false` leaves the row and is still counted as ended.
N3 (nit) — the ninth name joining the one-holder list tightens one requirement (a second package's override of `auth.password_changed_notice` is refused) under `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset says so in words, and the earlier built-in template shipped as `none`/`patch`; the seat confirms the kind at ACCEPT.
N4 (nit) — the reminder lists every unrevoked key as active, expired and inactive ones included, and reads one page of 500.

Per file, where no finding is listed above: `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts` holds against `resolveApiKeyAdmission` (apart from S4) and the vendor adapter; `auth-manager-before-hook.ts` returns early on an ended link ahead of checks that judge other paths; `auth-manager-email-sms-delivery.ts` and `auth-manager.ts` mirror `sendChangeEmailNotice` and never throw; `operator-password-reset.ts` still refuses an account with no local password, so it creates no first password; `admin-user-endpoints.ts`, the CLI command, the core list and the templates agree with the code they describe; the tests drive the real routes and pin a control beside each behaviour.
